c.tagline: Silk Road oasis under the Rainbow Mountains.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis in town and Didi widely used; the Danxia geopark is ~30 km out, so hire a car or join a tour for that day trip.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 is for ambulance/medical and 119 is fire.

hood_desc: The walkable heart of Ganzhou around the Ming-era Drum Tower (Zhonglou), with Minzhu Street, the night market, shops and most hotels; the convenient base for first-timers.
The gateway town near the Zhangye Danxia National Geological Park about 30 km west, where travellers stay to catch sunrise and sunset over the striped Rainbow Mountains; all about the landscape.
The newer district around Zhangye West high-speed railway station, with modern hotels and wide avenues; convenient for HSR arrivals but quieter and away from the old core.
lodging: Hampton by Hilton Zhangye West Railway Station
Homeinn Plus Hotel (Zhangye West Railway Station)

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: City buses run from about 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM; taxis and Didi fill the late-night gap, and the Danxia geopark needs a car or tour bus.
transit.note: Zhangye has a city bus network and taxis but no metro; the Rainbow Mountains and other Silk Road sights lie outside town and are reached by car, tour or long-distance bus.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash or by mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat) on board (about 1 yuan); taxis are metered and Didi is widely used.

bus: Zhangye Bus Station — coaches to Jiuquan, Wuwei, Lanzhou and Xining

car.idp: Foreign licences/IDP not valid in China — hire a car with driver for the Danxia geopark

train: Zhangye West Railway Station — Lanzhou–Ürümqi high-speed line; Zhangye Station on the Lanzhou–Xinjiang line

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to city centre (timed to flights)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in mainland China; there is no need to tip in restaurants or taxis.

landmarks: Zhangye Danxia National Geopark (Rainbow Mountains)
Striped ochre, crimson and gold hills ripple to the horizon—China's celebrated Rainbow Mountains, at their most photogenic in low sunset light.
Giant Buddha Temple (Dafo Si)
A Western Xia dynasty temple sheltering China's largest reclining clay Buddha, 34.5 serene meters of gilt beneath ancient timber halls.
Binggou Danxia
The Rainbow Mountains' quieter sibling, a labyrinth of castle-like pillars, windows and hoodoos sculpted from cream-and-rust sandstone.
Mati Si (Horse Hoof Temple)
Buddhist grottoes gouged into a sheer cliff face and linked by ladders and tunnels, backed by snowcapped Qilian peaks and Yugur culture.
Zhangye Wooden Pagoda
A nine-story wooden pagoda first raised in the Sui dynasty anchors the old town square, elegantly floodlit after dark.
Zhangye National Wetland Park
A surprising oasis of reed beds, boardwalks and migratory birds on the Heihe River, fringing the desert city's northern edge.
Pingshanhu Grand Canyon
A Gobi-edge canyon of buttes and hoodoos dubbed China's Grand Canyon, with rim walks and dramatic staircase descents to the floor.
Shandan Military Horse Ranch
One of the world's oldest and largest horse ranches, breeding cavalry mounts since the Han dynasty amid vast Qilian mountain meadows.
Zhenyuan Tower (Zhangye Drum Tower)
The Ming-era drum tower marks the central crossroads of the old Silk Road garrison town, elegant under evening lights.
Han and Ming Great Wall at Shandan
Rammed-earth stretches of Han and Ming dynasty Great Wall run side by side near Shandan, raw and crowd-free on the Hexi Corridor.

train.note: Zhangye has no international trains; the nearest border crossing by rail is the Urumqi to Almaty service, roughly a day further west. Zhangye West station handles the fast D-trains on the Lanzhou-Xinjiang high-speed railway, putting Lanzhou around 2.5 hours away and Xining, Jiayuguan, Xi'an and Urumqi within a comfortable day. The older Zhangye station takes about 49 daily conventional trains towards Beijing, Chongqing and the Hexi Corridor, but seats on long-distance through trains that merely pass through are notoriously hard to get. Book on 12306 with your passport as soon as the 15-day window opens, especially in the July-September Danxia season.

bus.note: There are no international coach services. Zhangye has three bus stations with distinct roles: the West station for the Qicai Danxia rainbow-hills scenic area and Xining, the East station for Wuwei and Lanzhou, and the South station for Dunhuang, Jiayuguan and other Hexi Corridor towns. Buses are the practical option for Dunhuang-area detours and for reaching Danxia and the Mati Si grottoes, where no train goes. Tickets are counter-only with a passport, and services thin out sharply in winter.

ferry.note: Zhangye is a desert oasis city in the Hexi Corridor, about as far from the sea as anywhere in China, and has no passenger boat services.

full.name: Jiayuguan
full.blurb: Westernmost fort of the Great Wall, a Ming-dynasty garrison guarding the historic Silk Road pass.

full.name: Wuwei
full.blurb: Former Silk Road garrison city with a Ming-dynasty bell tower and Han-dynasty tomb where the Flying Horse bronze was found.
